content.comment_body: Hello, I'm planning to regulate the temperature in a water tank using a PT100 sensor. I have the PT100 module for [product_name]. My goal is to switch on a refrigerator if the temperature exceeds a certain threshold (e.g. 28°C) and activate a heater if the temperature falls below another threshold (e.g. 25°C). Could this be managed using just one analog input, by handling both threshold checks via programming? Or is it necessary to use two analog inputs? Thank you. Bye, [user_name]

Once the analog input value is above 279, the threshold trigger's output is 'high', and this activates the refrigerator. At this point, the heating switches off because the 'high' signal is linked to the negative input of the 'AND' condition. So, when the analog value is above 279, only Q1 is active; when it drops below 251, Q2 becomes active. This ensures only one output is on at any moment. Does this align with what you're aiming for? The main topic is whether a single analog input can manage both heating and cooling functions by programming upper and lower temperature thresholds, and clarifying the logic for mutually exclusive output activation based on those thresholds.
